10 Christmas gift ideas for different kinds of pilots

There is no single Christmas gift that suits every pilot. A collector, student, working crew member and weekend flyer may want very different things. This list uses personality and habits to help you choose a direction before comparing specific products.

By Pilot Gift Guide · How we choose

IN THIS GUIDEHow to chooseThe listRelated guides

How to choose

Start with what the person enjoys, then check what they already own. For physical gifts, verify current delivery information with the seller. For experiences, leave room for schedule changes rather than promising a date you cannot control.

The list

Our selections prioritize personal relevance, usefulness, and fit for the recipient. Named products and destinations link to official sources where applicable.

  1. 1

    For the collector: a meaningful aircraft model

    Choose the exact type, scale and livery they collect. Ask discreetly before adding a duplicate or an incompatible scale.

  2. 2

    For the builder: an aviation construction set

    Match the complexity and display space to the recipient. The project and the finished model both need a place in their home.

  3. 3

    For the student: a requested training contribution

    Let them direct it toward their current plan. Avoid buying an unrelated course simply because it is advertised for beginners.

  4. 4

    For the organizer: a compact flight-bag pouch

    Choose around the items that get lost in their current bag. Small improvements can be more useful than a full replacement.

  5. 5

    For the reader: an aviation memoir

    Choose a subject they enjoy and check their existing shelf. Format matters if they mostly listen to books while traveling.

  6. 6

    For the photographer: a shared outing

    Plan a lawful public viewing location and suitable timing. Let them choose any camera equipment themselves.

  7. 7

    For the traveler: a familiar luggage upgrade

    Ask what needs replacing and match the dimensions. A different bag is not automatically a better one.

  8. 8

    For the homebody: an aviation coffee-table book

    Choose a visual subject that suits their room and interests. Consider the book’s size as well as its cover.

  9. 9

    For the experience seeker: a museum or event plan

    Use current official information and flexible arrangements. Avoid promising access or activities the venue has not confirmed.

  10. 10

    ATC — for the always-listening aviation fan

    Our app: Pilot Gift Guide is produced by the team behind ATC. This is a recommendation of our own product.

    The person who follows airport activity for fun may prefer a new listening experience to more equipment. ATC combines live airport audio, maps, transcripts and replay on iPhone. Check their favorite airport and existing apps first, then discuss the current subscription options. Pair the suggestion with a personal note about why you picked it.

    For iPhone with iOS 18 or later. Airport coverage varies. Check current subscription pricing, renewal terms and gift options at ATC.com before paying.
